links.note: The first Stundists still took communion in Orthodox churches, F. C. Conybeare wrote in 1921. Only about 1870 did they form a separate sect, and they baptized again anyone who joined them from Orthodoxy. In 1880 the historian Julian Pelesz listed the Stundists among the new sects that had left the Russian church.

prose_changes.old: Grew from the Stundist Bible-study movement among Ukrainian peasants in the 1860s and the Pashkovite circle in St Petersburg from 1874, joining as the Russian Baptist Union in 1884. Persecuted under the ober-procurator Konstantin Pobedonostsev, and in tension with the Russian Orthodox Church of the same era. These congregations are the direct ancestors of the Soviet-era Initsiativniki Baptist movement that followed.
prose_changes.new: It grew from two roots. In the 1860s Ukrainian peasants began to meet to study the Bible, and their neighbors called them Stundists. From 1874 a second circle met in St Petersburg around Vasily Pashkov. Their leaders met in 1884 to unite, but the police broke up the meeting. That year the Baptist churches of the south formed a Russian Baptist Union, while Pashkov's followers stayed apart. Konstantin Pobedonostsev, the lay official who ran the Orthodox Church for the tsar, led the state's campaign against them. They had left that church, and to leave it was a crime. Their churches are the ancestors of the Soviet-era Initsiativniki Baptists.
prose_changes.reason: 'Joining as the Russian Baptist Union in 1884' is wrong: the movement's own story has the police break up the 1884 St Petersburg congress, and the Pashkovites and Baptists stay two streams until 1944 (sources there: police records, Korff's memoir, Heier 1970, Coleman 2005). 'Of the same era' is a layout phrase, now said in words with the break. 'Direct' dropped: the descent runs through the 1944 union. Whole field rewritten in shorter sentences to meet the reading target.

prose_changes.old: In the 1860s Ukrainian peasants working alongside German colonists in the southern provinces began meeting for the Bible studies their neighbors called Stunden, hours — reading the Scriptures for themselves in the Russian translation then appearing. Reading became conversion, and conversion became congregations. The movement then met a second one coming from the opposite end of society. From 1874 in St Petersburg, aristocrats converted under the preaching of the English evangelist Lord Radstock gathered around Colonel Vasily Pashkov, who opened his house for meetings that servants and nobles attended together. The strands joined in a Russian Baptist Union in 1884, and the state answered with everything it had — Pashkov exiled, meetings broken up, children removed from Stundist parents, families deported. Since leaving the Orthodox Church was a crime as well as a sin. The toleration decree of 1905 gave them their first legal breathing space in forty years.
prose_changes.new: In the 1860s Ukrainian peasants in the south worked beside German colonists. They began meeting for Bible studies that their neighbors called Stunden, hours. They read the Bible for themselves, in the Russian translation then coming out. Reading became conversion, and conversion became congregations. Then the movement met a second one, coming from the other end of society. From 1874 in St Petersburg, nobles won by the preaching of the English evangelist Lord Radstock gathered around Colonel Vasily Pashkov. He opened his house to meetings where servants and nobles sat side by side. In 1884 Pashkov invited the leaders of every strand to his house to unite. On the fourth day the police broke up the meeting. That same year the Baptist churches of the south formed a Russian Baptist Union. Pashkov's followers stayed a separate stream. The state answered with everything it had. Pashkov was sent into exile and meetings were broken up. Children were taken from Stundist parents, and whole families were deported. Leaving the Orthodox Church was a crime as well as a sin. The toleration decree of 1905 gave them their first legal breathing space in forty years.
prose_changes.reason: Same correction as the summary: the strands did not join in 1884 (the movement's own story and its sources). The closing fragment beginning 'Since' is made a sentence. The rest is recast in shorter sentences to meet the reading target, with no fact added or dropped.
